name: Three-Color Process
description: Three monochrome glass records find their way back into color. A hands-on optical laboratory for additive photographic reconstruction.

assets.credit: Original optical-laboratory composition; historical exposure records from Library of Congress
assets.license: MIT treatment; no known restrictions on archival photographs

assets.credit: Sergei Mikhailovich Prokudin-Gorskii, Mosaics on walls in Old Bukhara, between 1905 and 1915. Library of Congress, LC-DIG-prok-01876. Prepared from the actual three-exposure scan; see archive-preparation.json and ASSET-LICENSES.txt.
Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Prokudin-Gorskii Collection, LC-DIG-prok-01876

compatibility: WebGL with fragment high precision is preferred; Canvas 2D supplies a smaller preview when WebGL is unavailable. PNG export uses the same linear-light CPU engine in either case.
Pointer, touch, keyboard and numeric registration controls. No motion or automatic playback is required.
Local JPEG, PNG and WebP selection; maximum 25 MB file, decoded working image capped to 1,280 pixels on its longest side. Browser decode memory still depends on the input dimensions.
Images are decoded into a canvas explicitly requesting sRGB. Wide-gamut images are converted to sRGB; this is not a raw-film density or color-calibrated archival-restoration tool.
Idle projection uses no animation loop. Hidden/offscreen automatic alignment stops; disposal releases textures, buffers, context, canvases, object URLs, observers and listeners.
notes: The historical sample uses distinct blue/green/red records from an original Prokudin-Gorskii scan. Grayscale crops are registered and contrast-normalized during asset preparation, with no local retouching. Remaining damage and small warping differences are retained.
The main surface simulates additive colored light on a screen. Glass frames are an interaction metaphor; ordinary colored transparent sheets do not recreate this projection by physical stacking.

Modern photographs split into genuine R/G/B intensity records. sRGB transfer functions are decoded before exposure, interpolation and fringe adjustments, then encoded once for display. Neutral aligned output closely matches the decoded source.

The three thumbnails always show original monochrome records. Inspect any record in grayscale or through its corresponding filter. Selection and frame stacking never change the arithmetic channel sum.
Align restores known shared origins: the modern image split or the supplied historical calibration. It does not claim to automatically recover arbitrary unknown historical geometry.
Fringe intensity adjusts the linear-light difference between moved and registered records. One is the faithful reconstruction; other values are labeled artistic settings.
reuse: Use separate / fromRecords and reconstruct in model.js for CPU reconstruction, or createPlateRenderer for an interactive GPU projection.
The exported example.html and embed-demo.html run through a static HTTP server without packages, a CDN or Tampa page code.
Presets and alignment JSON contain settings only. Local image pixels are never uploaded or included in source packages; reselect the matching file after reload.
README.md defines coordinate transforms, sRGB handling, exports, record preparation, validation and resource disposal.
